content: 1. The concurrent use of cefditoren with other medications may necessitate an additional form of birth control. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Cefditoren may reduce the therapeutic effects of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 3. Doxycycline can decrease the effects of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 4. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 6. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 8. Erythromycin stearate can decrease the effects of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 9. Cefditoren may reduce the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Famotidine may decrease the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance, but there is an increased risk of nephrotoxicity. Monitor closely. 12. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of gentamicin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 13. Ibuprofen/famotidine may decrease the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of kanamycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 15. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antibacterial agents may decrease the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 16. Minocycline can decrease the effects of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 17. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of neomycin (oral) through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 18. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 19. Nizatidine may decrease the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 21. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 22. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of plazomicin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 23. Probenecid may increase the levels or effects of cefditoren by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 25. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cefditoren by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. Monitor closely. 26. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 27. Sodium bicarbonate may decrease the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration with antibiotics may decrease efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. 29. Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate may decrease the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer drugs at least 2 hours before or after sodium zirconium cyclosilicate. 30. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of streptomycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 31. Tetracycline can decrease the effects of cefditoren due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 32. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 33. Cefditoren may increase the toxicity of tobramycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 34. Cefditoren may reduce the effects of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors may interfere with their therapeutic efficacy. 35. Cefditoren and voclosporin may each increase the toxicity of the other through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Co-administration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 36. Cefditoren may increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Willow bark may increase the levels or effects of cefditoren by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 38. Common adverse effects of cefditoren include diarrhea (11–15%), nausea (4–6%), headache (2–3%), abdominal pain (2%), dyspepsia (1–2%), and vomiting (1%). 39. Other potential adverse effects include bacterial or fungal superinfection, Clostridioides difficile colitis, hypersensitivity reactions, increased bleeding time, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, and vaginal moniliasis (yeast infection). 40. Cefditoren is contraindicated in individuals with documented hypersensitivity to the drug, penicillin, related compounds, or milk protein sodium caseinate, as well as those with carnitine deficiency or inborn errors of metabolism that may result in clinically significant carnitine deficiency. 41. Prolonged use of cefditoren may lead to diarrhea, nausea, vaginal moniliasis, pseudomembranous colitis, clinical manifestations of carnitine deficiency, and the emergence or overgrowth of resistant organisms. 42. Use caution when prescribing cefditoren to breastfeeding individuals. Its excretion in breast milk is unknown. 43. Cefditoren is classified as Pregnancy Category B, indicating that controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 44. Cefditoren is a semi-synthetic cephalosporin administered as a prodrug. It is hydrolyzed by esterases during absorption and distributed in the bloodstream as active cefditoren. 45. Its bactericidal activity results from the inhibition of cell wall synthesis via affinity for penicillin-binding proteins. 46. Cefditoren is excreted primarily in the urine, with a half-life of 1.5–3 hours.
